updates.title: GitHub separates BYOK usage in Copilot reports
updates.whatChanged: GitHub added local BYOK usage fields and enterprise custom-model flags to Copilot usage metrics on 4 November. Reports now separate these requests at user and aggregate levels in 1-day and 28-day views. Local BYOK fields rely on client telemetry and may undercount.
updates.whyCare: You can separate Copilot-hosted usage from local provider keys, local models and enterprise custom models, then check activity against policy. Local BYOK counts can miss requests when client telemetry is disabled.
updates.before: Copilot reports included BYOK in broader client totals, which could mix local or custom-model use with GitHub-hosted models.
updates.after: Reports identify local BYOK activity and flag enterprise custom-model requests, with user-level and aggregate counts across 1-day and 28-day views.
updates.learn: Update Copilot dashboards to separate local BYOK and enterprise custom-model use. Check telemetry coverage and token-count gaps before comparing costs or enforcing policy.

sources.name: GitHub Changelog - BYOK and enterprise custom models in the Copilot usage API
GitHub Docs - Copilot usage metrics API

updates.architectureImplication: Use Copilot usage records as a multi-provider cost and policy feed. Join user-level BYOK metrics to approved-provider inventories, and account for the local telemetry blind spot.
heldReasons: Fact check: The item dates the announcement November 4; the GitHub changelog identifies it as November 3, published at 16:32 -08:00.
